Two declarations state Lemma 4.11: TrueConeLoopPaper.exists_local_family_with_margin and its global-data form in TrueConeLoop. With m = t_s and C = −b_L, the Lean hypotheses are exactly (4.20)–(4.21) on the rectangle plus v_s > 2 on the end faces, and the conclusions are the period-one family, the mean (a, −b_s), the admissible cone at every φ with p_s fixed, a uniform positive margin, and φ-independence near the radial boundary. The two departures are encoding: the margin lives in the (4.21) coordinates rather than the Ψ of (4.35) (bridged by ConeAlgebra.true_cone_iff plus compactness), and smoothness is assumed on an open neighbourhood rather than on the closed rectangle. Both are low and conventional; the Lean statement is otherwise more general.

findings.summary: Lean's uniform margin is in the (4.21) coordinates — ε ≤ P_c − 2 and ε ≤ U(P_c,J_c) − v — not the paper's Ψ of (4.35), whose third and fourth gaps are P_c − v and 2(P_c−v)² − (v−2)J_c².

The Lean hypotheses require the data smooth on an open set containing the parameter rectangle (or globally); the paper requires smoothness only on the closed rectangle I × [−1,1], with one-sided derivatives at η = ±1.
